**Discpress 1.3.4 makes the downloaded file as careful with your results as the online version.** Chrome and Edge give a page opened as a file no disk storage of its own, so there Discpress keeps results in memory, and a reload used to lose them without a word.

## Get it

- **[⬇ discpress.html](https://github.com/PowerBeef/discpress/releases/download/v1.3.4/discpress.html)** (about 2.9 MB): the whole app in one file you keep.
- **[🌐 powerbeef.github.io/discpress](https://powerbeef.github.io/discpress/)**: nothing to download, and the way to convert big games on iPhone and iPad.

## Changes

- **Results lost to a reload are named.** Where results live in memory, the next visit says which results were lost, and how to keep them next time: save each one when it's ready, have results written into a folder (Chrome and Edge), or use Discpress online, where results stay on disk until you save them.
- **A conversion cut off by a reload is reported** there too, as it already was online.
- **The note about memory says what it means:** closing or reloading loses the results not saved yet. It only offers the options your browser has.
- **Several open tabs no longer confuse each other's records** of unsaved results.
- **README and Help** say which browsers keep a downloaded file's results in memory.

The CHDs are the same as 1.3.0's.
